title: Symphony No. 9 in D minor, “Choral”
hook: The symphony that found it needed the human voice.

painting.title: Morning (first version), also called The Small Morning
painting.pairingNote: A radiant vision of light and new beginning from Beethoven’s own generation, matching the finale’s hymn to joy.

facts: First performed on 7 May 1824 in Vienna. Beethoven, by then deaf, had to be turned around to see the applause.
The first major symphony to include singers. The finale sets Friedrich Schiller’s poem “Ode to Joy”.
The order of the middle movements is reversed: the fast [[scherzo|scherzo]] comes second and the slow movement third.
The finale begins by quoting, and rejecting, each of the earlier movements before the joy theme is found.
bigPicture.inOneLine: creation out of chaos (I), wild energy (II), deep peace (III), a search that ends in song (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro ma non troppo, un poco maestoso
movements.tempo: Allegro ma non troppo, un poco maestoso
movements.summary: The music seems to form out of nothing: a hollow shimmer, falling fragments, then a theme of enormous force. A vast [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement.

mainIdeas.name: The shimmer
mainIdeas.description: a bare, empty-sounding hum in the strings, neither major nor minor.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a jagged line crashing downward, played by the whole orchestra together.

stops.hear: A quiet, hollow shimmer; small fragments drop through it
stops.happening: The opening. Like an orchestra tuning, or a world taking shape

stops.hear: The fragments gather and crash down in [[unison|unison]]
stops.happening: Theme 1, fortissimo

stops.hear: Warm, gentle phrases in the woodwinds
stops.happening: The second group of themes, in a major key. A first hint of the shape of the joy tune

stops.hear: The hollow shimmer returns
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins. It sounds like a repeat, but soon goes elsewhere

stops.hear: The shimmer comes back as a roar: full orchestra over thundering drums
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]. What was a whisper is now a catastrophe, and in the major key, which makes it more frightening, not less

stops.hear: Low strings grind out a creeping figure, over and over
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]], like a funeral procession

stops.label: Last bars
stops.hear: Theme 1 one final time, in unison
stops.happening: An ending with no comfort

notice: Compare the first seconds with the stop at ≈ 8:30. It is the same music at opposite extremes.

movements.heading: Molto vivace – Presto
movements.summary: A [[scherzo|scherzo]] driven by a single leaping rhythm, with the drums as soloist.

stops.hear: Three hammered leaps, the second one by the timpani alone
stops.happening: The call to attention. At the premiere the audience reportedly applauded here

stops.hear: A quiet, skittering tune that spreads from one string section to the next
stops.happening: A [[fugato|fugato]] built on the leaping rhythm

stops.label: Middle of the scherzo
stops.hear: The drums keep interrupting, loudly, on their own
stops.happening: Beethoven uses the timpani as a comic and violent solo voice

stops.hear: A smooth, folk-like tune in oboes and clarinets over a bustling bassoon
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]], in D major. Trombones enter the symphony here

stops.label: After the trio
stops.hear: The skittering music returns
stops.happening: The scherzo is repeated

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: The trio starts again and is cut off
stops.happening: A joke ending

movements.heading: Adagio molto e cantabile
movements.summary: The still centre of the symphony. Two melodies alternate, and the first becomes more richly decorated each time it returns.

stops.hear: A slow hymn in the strings; woodwinds echo the end of each phrase
stops.happening: Theme A

stops.hear: A flowing, slightly faster melody in the second violins and violas
stops.happening: Theme B, in a brighter key

stops.hear: The hymn returns with the violins weaving ornaments around it
stops.happening: First [[variation|variation]] of Theme A

stops.label: Middle
stops.hear: A horn plays a slow, exposed scale on its own
stops.happening: A famous solo for the fourth horn

stops.hear: The hymn in long, floating lines of running notes
stops.happening: The fullest variation

stops.label: and again shortly after
stops.hear: Trumpets and drums break in with a stern fanfare
stops.happening: Twice the dream is interrupted, as if by a wake-up call. Each time the calm returns

movements.heading: Finale
movements.summary: A drama in several scenes: chaos, a search through the past, the discovery of a simple tune, and finally voices. The form is unlike anything before it.

stops.hear: A harsh, clashing blast from winds and drums
stops.happening: The “terror fanfare”

stops.hear: Cellos and basses alone, speaking like a singer without words
stops.happening: An instrumental [[recitative|recitative]]

stops.hear: Short quotations of movements I, II and III, each cut off by the basses
stops.happening: The past is tried and rejected

stops.hear: Cellos and basses, very quietly, play a simple tune
stops.happening: The joy theme, heard for the first time, unaccompanied

stops.hear: The tune repeats, each time with more instruments, up to the full orchestra
stops.happening: Three [[variation|variation]]s

stops.hear: The terror fanfare again; then a solo baritone
stops.happening: “O friends, not these sounds!” The first words in any Beethoven symphony

stops.hear: Baritone, then chorus, sing the joy theme
stops.happening: The Ode to Joy begins

stops.hear: A huge held chord on the words “vor Gott”
stops.happening: The first great climax; then silence

stops.hear: Thumps from bass drum and bassoon; piccolo, triangle and cymbals; a tenor sings
stops.happening: A “Turkish” march: the joy theme as a jaunty military band

stops.hear: Orchestra alone, fast and tangled
stops.happening: An orchestral [[fugue|fugue]]

stops.hear: Full chorus and orchestra burst out with the joy theme
stops.happening: The most famous statement

stops.hear: Men’s voices and trombones in a broad, solemn new theme
stops.happening: “Be embraced, you millions”. A second, hymn-like idea

stops.hear: High, hushed, shimmering chords
stops.happening: “Above the stars he must dwell”. The mystical heart of the finale

stops.hear: Sopranos sing the joy theme while altos sing the solemn theme at the same time
stops.happening: A double [[fugue|fugue]] combining both ideas

stops.hear: The four soloists alone, slow and ornate; the soprano climbs very high
stops.happening: A vocal [[cadenza|cadenza]]

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Everything accelerates wildly
stops.happening: The Prestissimo close

notice: The joy theme moves almost entirely by step. Anyone can sing it, which is the point.
The finale repeats the symphony’s opening idea: something simple growing, layer by layer, from near silence.

threads.title: From nothing to everything
threads.body: Both the first movement and the joy theme begin in a whisper and grow to the full orchestra.

threads.title: Rejection and discovery
threads.body: The finale openly dismisses the earlier movements; words arrive when instruments are no longer enough.

threads.title: D minor to D major
threads.body: As in the Fifth, the symphony is a journey from dark to light.
